ai_show_review.summary: Raw 1969 set with rare Jerry‑lead Good Lovin' and exploratory jams
ai_show_review.blurb: The show delivers a standout Jerry vocal on Good Lovin', a gritty Big Boy Pete, and an adventurous He Was A Friend Of Mine. While the early tracks are low‑volume and the pacing can feel sluggish, the raw energy of this late‑summer gig makes it worth a listen.
ai_show_review.review: On September 6, 1969 at the Family Dog, the Dead offered a raw, uneven performance that still shines through on several key moments. Jerry Garcia’s guitar is rock‑solid and his lead vocal on Good Lovin' has been called “fabulous,” while his thick, twangy solo on He Was A Friend Of Mine adds an exploratory edge. The set also features the rare inclusion of Big Boy Pete and a double‑take on All Over Now (both the Dylan cover and the Baby Blue rendition). Though the first three tracks suffer from low volume and tape hiss, the later portion of the soundboard capture is clear enough to enjoy the band’s compelling energy despite missing classic 1969 staples like Dark Star or St. Stephen. Pigpen’s harmonica work gets a nod on one of the lesser‑documented recordings, adding an extra flavor for completists.

best_recording.reason: Solid soundboard with good overall mix; captures the standout songs and Jerry’s lead vocal despite early volume issues.
